extracted.intended_audience: NLP / argument mining researchers and engineers developing or evaluating argument classification systems
extracted.subtask_description: Designing, training, and evaluating models to classify argumentative components and relations (e.g., claims/premises, support/attack/no-relation) using compact transformer models (BERT/DistilBERT) with selective LLM (GPT-4) refinement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Argument mining subtask decomposition
rubrics_metrics.description: The whole task can be decomposed into three main sub-tasks: (1) identification of argument components — distinguishing argumentative propositions from non-argumentative propositions (segmentation); (2) identification of clausal properties — finding premises or conclusions among the argumentative propositions; (3) identification of relational properties — given two argumentative propositions, identify which type of relation links them (support, attack, no relation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design datasets, models, and evaluation to reflect these three distinct subtasks (component detection, clause-type classification, pairwise relation classification). Each subtask can be solved with classification models and may require different inputs (e.g., single sentence vs. (thesis, claim) pair).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use diverse, comparative datasets
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct comparative studies across a wide spectrum of datasets rather than on a single dataset; this paper uses Args.me, UKP, and US2016.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-dataset evaluation helps reveal model generality and dataset-specific issues. When possible include multiple domains (debate portals, online comments, debate transcripts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dataset label schemes and class definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt and report the dataset-specific label schemes: US2016 uses RA (Inference), CA (Conflict), MA (Rephrase), NO (No Relation); UKP uses supporting / opposing / non-argument; Args.me annotations include conclusions and premises, split into PRO premises and CON premises (and PRO/CON conclusions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about the label set used for each dataset and ensure the model output dimension matches the number of classes. Report experiments both with and without conclusion context where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annotator agreement threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: For UKP the sentences were annotated by 7 annotators and 'for each classification, it was necessary to achieve agreement, as measured by Cohen’s kappa (κ), at the level of 0.723; this exceeds the commonly used threshold of 0.7 for assuming the results are reliable.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Cohen's kappa (or another agreement measure) and target κ ≥ 0.7 as a minimum reliability threshold for annotation quality; report inter-annotator agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compact language model classifier architecture
rubrics_metrics.description: Classifiers are built by adding fully connected layers at the output of transformer-based models (DistilBERT, BERT). Two fully connected layers are added at the top of the Transformer blocks; the output size of the last fully connected layer equals the number of classes to recognize. (C_Θc(X) = f_θ2(f_θ1(T_Θ(X))))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using CLMs, implement small classification heads (e.g., two dense layers) on the transformer encoder output; ensure final layer dimension equals class count and follow standard fine-tuning steps (compute loss, backpropagate gradients, update Θc).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hybrid CLM + LLM refinement algorithm (uncertainty routing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Train a compact classifier C_Θc on the dataset; compute per-instance uncertainty/loss differences Λ = {|C_Θc(Xb) - Yb|} across training (or validation) to select a threshold γ; for instances with model uncertainty above γ, route them to a large language model (LLM) (ChatGPT-4) for re-evaluation; otherwise use the CLM's prediction. (Algorithm 1)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement a pipeline that (1) builds/trains the base CLM, (2) computes an uncertainty measure for instances, (3) chooses γ to select the top-k uncertain instances, and (4) delegates those to an LLM while letting CLM handle the rest. Log delegation rates and downstream effect on accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gamma selection / delegation rate guideline
rubrics_metrics.description: Set γ so that a limited fraction of instances with highest uncertainty are delegated to the LLM. Example settings used: Args.me — approximately 20% of arguments delegated; US2016 — γ set so that 25% of the data with lowest confidence were delegated to ChatGPT-4.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tune γ (delegation fraction) to trade off improved accuracy versus LLM usage cost. Typical explored ranges in this work were ~20–25% of highest-uncertainty examples. Report the chosen γ and its effect on both accuracy and LLM call volume.

rubrics_metrics.name: LLM prompting template for refinement
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a simple input-output prompting template for GPT-4: "This is a thesis '...'. And this is a claim '...'. Is the claim an argument for or contra the thesis? Write a one-sentence answer."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide both thesis and claim as input (rather than claim alone) — experiments showed better results when the argument and a thesis were given as input. Keep the prompt concise and task-focused; consider more advanced prompting later (e.g., Tree of Thoughts) for improved reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation metrics to report
rubrics_metrics.description: Report Top-1 accuracy and F1 (mean F1 where appropriate) as primary evaluation metrics (tables show top1 and F1 across datasets and models).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide both Top-1 accuracy and class-balanced F1 (or mean F1) to capture overall correctness and per-class performance; show results per-dataset and aggregated (e.g., mean F1 across thematic subsets).

rubrics_metrics.name: Include context (thesis/conclusion) when available
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing an argument together with its thesis (conclusion) as input produced better results in experiments than providing only the argument text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When dataset affords a thesis/conclusion, include it in the model input for classification tasks (e.g., pair (thesis, claim)); compare performance with argument-only inputs and report gains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benchmark and expected performance improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: The hybrid BERT+ChatGPT-4 model outperformed DistilBERT and BERT standalone models across datasets; improvements reported often exceeded ~10% in F1 and substantial Top-1 gains (e.g., Args.me top1: DistilBERT 65.1 → BERT 76.22 → BERT+ChatGPT-4 85.87; F1: 68.9 → 71.5 → 87.2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the hybrid approach as a baseline when reporting results; report absolute values and percentage improvements over base CLMs. Provide per-dataset numbers and the delegation rate used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common LLM error modes to analyze and report
rubrics_metrics.description: Observed GPT-4 failure modes include: difficulty processing logical connectives; failure to detect sarcasm/irony; incorrect classification on sentences with multiple negations; mistakes arising from context mismatch (issues placed in atypical contexts); cases where the LLM contradicts itself when asked to justify an incorrect answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform qualitative error analysis on LLM-refined predictions, document typical failure patterns with examples, and consider these patterns when designing prompts and post-processing checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dataset quality and label noise considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Some datasets contain incorrect or controversial human labels (e.g., UKP contains ~10% incorrect/problematic classifications). In some such cases, GPT's evaluations appeared more consistent with reality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess dataset label quality; consider auditing or relabeling noisy subsets; report label-noise estimates and analyze how label noise affects both CLM and LLM behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data size effect on fine-tuning
rubrics_metrics.description: Results are generally better for the largest subsets (more training examples). The paper notes better results for larger UKP thematic subsets (e.g., abortion, nuclear energy) because 'the model has a larger number of training courses, which allows it to better perform the fine-tuning process.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect performance to scale with available labeled data. When possible, augment smaller domains or perform transfer/cross-domain learning; report per-subset sizes alongside performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Efficiency / resource trade-offs
rubrics_metrics.description: Compact language models (CLMs) have fewer parameters, making them faster to run and easier to deploy in resource-constrained environments; LLMs are computationally expensive. The hybrid approach aims to minimize LLM usage by invoking the LLM only for a selected subset of uncertain inputs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design systems to prioritize CLM inference and selectively call LLMs for uncertain cases to reduce latency and cost. Report compute and latency trade-offs as well as total percentage of instances delegated to LLM.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility: report compute environment
rubrics_metrics.description: All experiments were executed on a workstation equipped with Nvidia Tesla V100-SXM2-32GB GPUs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report hardware used for training and inference (GPU type and memory) to aid reproducibility and to contextualize training/fine-tuning speed claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider future improvements in LLM prompting and open-source options
rubrics_metrics.description: Future work recommends exploring open-source large models (e.g., Llama-2) and more advanced prompting techniques (e.g., Tree of Thoughts) to enhance GPT-based refinement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When extending the pipeline, evaluate open-source LLMs for cost/accessibility and test structured prompting or multi-step reasoning prompts to reduce LLM error modes and improve reasoning on complex argument structures.
